predecessors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
predecessors.text: the Umayyad Caliphate, taken in three stages: Khurasan (Merv, 14 February 748), Iraq (Kufa, 2 September 749; the Zab, January 750) and Syria and Egypt (Damascus in April 750; Marwan II killed in…

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: Baghdad and the Sawad, the caliph's last land, sacked by Hulagu's army in February 1258

successors.name: Ilkhanate
successors.text: Baghdad and southern Iraq, from 1258 under Hulagu, whose khanate later became the Ilkhanate

ledger.x: 749: al-Saffah is recognised as caliph in the mosque at Kufa.
749: Marwan II marches against the new caliph.
750: the Iranian plateau south and east of the 749 core, with Fars, Kirman, Sistan, Makran and the Sindh edge, is Abbasid by the time of Cliopatria's 750 shape.
750: the Abbasids win at the Zab.
750: Iraq is Abbasid.
750: Damascus falls to the Abbasids.
750: the rest of the Umayyad dominions pass to the Abbasids.
750: Marwan II is killed in Egypt.
751: the Abbasids defeat a Tang army at Talas.
755: Transoxiana is consolidated.
759: al-Mansur's armies enter Tabaristan.
760: the fighting for Tabaristan ends; Khurshid, who 'invaded Tabaristan in 760' from Daylam, is repulsed.
760: Tabaristan becomes an Abbasid province.
761: Ifriqiya returns to Abbasid rule.
762: al-Mansur founds Baghdad.
763: the Khazar-facing Caucasus edge is lost.
768: the Caucasus edge is back under the caliph.
800: Harun al-Rashid makes Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab hereditary emir of Ifriqiya.
814: Iberia (Georgia) leaves the shape.
814: the Abbasids beat the Turk Shahis.
816: the Turk Shahi submits.
819: the sons of Asad ibn Saman are made governors in the east.
821: Tahir is made governor of Khorasan, founding the Tahirids.
825: Armenia and Azerbaijan are lost to rebels and local rulers.
836: al-Mu'tasim founds Samarra.
837: the Khurramite rebellion ends and Azerbaijan returns.
860: Sindh slips from the caliph.
864: Tabaristan goes to the Zaydi Alids.
866: the Ziyadids hold part of Yemen under Abbasid allegiance.
869: the Zanj revolt begins around Basra.
870: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth takes Herat.
871: the Zanj take Basra.
873: the Saffarids end Tahirid rule.
873: Khorasan passes to the Saffarids.
873: al-Mu'tamid names Ahmad ibn Tulun governor of Egypt.
875: the Saffarids hold Fars, Kirman and Sistan.
876: the Zanj take the marshlands between Basra and Wasit.
878: Ahmad ibn Tulun takes Syria.
883: the Zanj revolt ends.
883: al-Muwaffaq's army retakes the Zanj country.
886: Armenia leaves the shape.
886: the eastern edge (Zabulistan and Sindh side) leaves the shape.
892: the seat returns to Baghdad.
898: more Saffarid land leaves the shape.
898: the Sajids hold Azerbaijan.
898: the Tulunids give up Aleppo and Qinnasrin.
899: the Qarmatians found their state in eastern Arabia.
899: the Arabian periphery leaves the shape.
900: the caliph invests Ismail ibn Ahmad with Khorasan, Tabaristan, Ray and Isfahan.
900: the caliph sends an army against the Qarmatians.

903: the Abbasid governor Ibn Banu claims Qatif in late 903 (his own report), but 'Hajar was forced to surrender anew to the Qarmatians after they cut its water supply'; the contest ends with the Qarmatians holding Bahrayn.
903: Hajar passes to the Qarmatians.
905: Abbasid troops overthrow the Tulunids in Egypt.
905: and in Syria.
905: Egypt and Syria return to the caliph's direct rule, six years before Cliopatria's 911 shape shows them.
909: the Kutama and the Fatimid cause take Ifriqiya from the Aghlabids.
914: the Fatimids take Cyrenaica.
929: Hasan Nasir al-Dawla is governor of Mosul and Diyar Bakr.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 931: Mardavij takes the Abbasid cities of the Jibal.
931: the rest of the Jibal of Cliopatria's Abbasid shape passes to Mardavij.
934: Ali ibn Buya conquers Fars.
934: Khuzestan passes to the Ziyarids.
935: Muhammad ibn Tughj is made governor of Egypt.
944: the caliph awards the Ikhshidids Egypt, Syria and the Hijaz for thirty years.
944: Edessa is reconquered by the Byzantines.
945: the Buyids take Baghdad.
946: the end of Cliopatria's Ziyadid allegiance relation (866-946); the Abbasid page does not mention the Ziyadids.
947: the Hamdanids are no longer the caliph's governors.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 962: the Makurians push into Upper Egypt.
964: the Makurian push ends; the page gives the span '962 and 964' and no battle.
969: the Fatimids conquer Egypt.
969: the Ikhshidid governorships of Syria and the Hijaz end with the dynasty.
969-970: no direct Abbasid land is left in Syria, Egypt or the Hejaz.
999: the Karakhanids take Bukhara.
999: the Samanid domains are divided.
999: the caliph's nominal hold on Khorasan ends with the Samanids.
1136: Iraq passes from the Seljuk sultans to the caliph's state; mirrors great-seljuk-empire /ledger/47.
1162: the caliph's army defeats the Mazyadids of Hilla.
1202: the Ayyubids acknowledge the caliph.
1202: the Sultanate of Rum acknowledges the caliph.
1210: the Delhi Sultanate acknowledges the caliph.
1249: the end of Cliopatria's Rum allegiance relation (1202-1249).
1250: the Mamluks seize power in Egypt.
1258: the Delhi allegiance ends with the caliphate.
1258: the Mongols take Baghdad.
1258: the Abbasid Caliphate ends with the sack of Baghdad.

wars.name: Abbasid Revolution
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: revolt from Merv on 9 June 747, Merv held from 14 February 748, Kufa 749, the Zab in January 750, Damascus in April and Marwan II killed in Egypt in August 750; the Umayyad state ends.

wars.name: Battle of Talas
wars.outcome: 'Gao Xianzhi and his army were defeated in 751 at the Battle of Talas': Tang influence in Transoxiana ends and the Abbasids consolidate there.

wars.name: Abbasid conquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: 'the Abbasids conquered his country in 759-760'; Tabaristan becomes a Caliphate province ruled from Amul, with the mountain dynasties as tributaries.

wars.name: Arab-Byzantine wars
wars.outcome: A frontier war with no border change on the page: al-Mahdi 'restarted the fighting' after 775, Harun al-Rashid's 'massive invasion of 806', a Byzantine attack on Syria repulsed around 829, Damietta sacked in 853, and the Abbasid frontier forces 'annihilated…

wars.name: Fourth Fitna
wars.outcome: 'After his death in 809, his succession pact eventually collapsed and the empire was split by a civil war'; 'When the city fell in 813, al-Amin was captured and executed'; al-Ma'mun reached Baghdad in August 819.

wars.name: Abbasid campaign against the Kabul Shahis
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory without annexation: the Turk Shahi pays 'an annual tribute of 1,500,000 dirhams and 2,000 slaves' and sends an idol to Mecca (816).

wars.name: Khurramite rebellion in Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: 'a rebellion in Azerbaijan by the Khurramites, supported by the Byzantines, which continued until 837': the caliph regains the land.

wars.name: Anarchy at Samarra
wars.outcome: 'The following period, sometimes known as the Anarchy at Samarra (861-870), saw four different caliphs come and go.'

wars.name: Zanj Rebellion
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: revolt from September 869; al-Ubulla 870, Suq al-Ahwaz and Basra 871, the marshes 876, furthest extent 879; al-Mukhtarah besieged February 881 and fallen August 883.

wars.name: Saffarid conquest of Khorasan
wars.outcome: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth takes Herat (870) and Nishapur and annexes Khorasan (873), ending Tahirid rule.

wars.name: Saffarid march on Baghdad
wars.outcome: Ya'qub's forces came close to overthrowing the Abbasids in 876, but the caliphal army halted them 'within a few days' march from Baghdad'; he was 'defeated by al-Muwaffaq'.

wars.name: Battle of Balkh (Samanid-Saffarid war)
wars.outcome: 'In 898, al-Mu'tadid set the Saffarids and Samanids against each other' (Abbasid page); Ismail defeated Amr at Balkh (900 on the Samanid page, 900 and 901 on the Saffarid page), sent him to Baghdad, and the caliph recognised Ismail as ruler of Khorasan and…

wars.name: Abbasid reconquest of Egypt and Syria
wars.outcome: 'In 905, the Tulunids were unable to resist an invasion by the Abbasid troops': direct caliphal rule returns in Syria and Egypt.

wars.name: Qarmatian wars
wars.outcome: The Qarmatians keep eastern Arabia (found 899), ambush the pilgrim caravan in 906, come close to Baghdad in 927, sack Mecca in 930 and take tribute from the caliph; the Abbasids paid for the Black Stone's return in 952 (the page gives 952).

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Iraq
wars.outcome: 'In 945, the youngest brother, Ahmad ibn Buya, conquered Iraq and made Baghdad his capital'; the caliph becomes a figurehead.

wars.name: Seljuk-Abbasid conflicts
wars.outcome: Al-Mustarshid lost to Sultan Mas'ud in 1135 and died in captivity; Mas'ud briefly retook Baghdad in 1136 and forced al-Rashid to abdicate; al-Muqtafi 'restored a high degree of independence' and resisted the Seljuk siege of 1157.

wars.name: Abbasid defeat of the Mazyadids of Hilla
wars.outcome: 'the Abbasids defeated the Mazyadids of Hilla in 1162'.

wars.name: Siege of Baghdad (1258)
wars.outcome: Mongol victory: the assault began on 29 or 30 January 1258, the caliph surrendered on 10 February, the sack began on 13 February and al-Musta'sim was executed on 20 February.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened.

sources.title: Byzantine Empire under the Macedonian dynasty
